call_overview.title: About the call
call_overview.question: What does the call offer, and who can apply?

cards.title: What the call wants
cards.question: What is the principal thing the project must develop, and which problem or need must it address?
cards.answer: Develop and demonstrate flexible manufacturing processes and machinery that can make both lithium-ion and sodium-ion battery cells at pilot scale.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 98–101 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 98–101 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Project impact
cards.question: Which wider system outcomes and impacts must the project support?
cards.answer: Cut production energy use and costs while maintaining cell quality. Flexible lines should make European battery production more competitive and resilient.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 98–101 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Who it suits
cards.question: Who may lead, which partners must take part, and how must the work be shared?
cards.answer: Battery-cell manufacturers and production-line equipment providers are well placed to lead projects with pilot lines and research partners. At least three independent grant recipients must be in different eligible countries, including one in a European Union Member State. Control by China or by an entity based there prevents participation.

cards.title: Innovation
cards.question: How new must the project be, and in what must it innovate?
cards.answer: Innovate in modular machinery, mixing and electrode production, dry-room assembly, cell formation (first charging that makes a cell usable) and in-line quality monitoring.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 98–101 · Scope

cards.title: Maturity
cards.question: Which maturity level is expected at the start and end of the project?
cards.answer: The work should reach TRL 6–7 (technology readiness level: technology demonstrated in relevant or operational conditions) by project end. The call allows work to start at any maturity level.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 98–101 · Specific conditions

cards.title: Demonstration and integration of work
cards.question: Where must the solution be demonstrated, and how must the work fit with existing systems?
cards.answer: Install and demonstrate reconfigurable machinery on pilot lines. Show how process steps and quality checks work together when production switches between the two battery chemistries.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 98–101 · Scope

call_overview.title: Relevance to TenneT
call_overview.question: Why is this call relevant to TenneT?

cards.title: Why it matters to TenneT
cards.question: Why does this call matter to TenneT, and why can't TenneT take part itself?
cards.answer: Lower-cost battery cells could improve the economics of future grid flexibility. The topic covers cell production and factory equipment and provides no transmission-operator role.

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
The Commission indicates EUR 37.8 million for lithium-ion and sodium-ion cell manufacturing. It expects 2 awards.
- Grant request: around EUR 18.9 million per project is indicative. The Commission can select a different request.
- Funding form: Budget-based grant (paid using approved costs or rates for the funded work).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 98–101 · Specific conditions

Sustainable and Competitive Cell Production Techniques for Lithium-ion And Sodium-ion Batteries (BATT4EU Partnership) · Budget overview

cards.title: Funding rate and co-financing
cards.answer:
For-profit organisations can receive up to 70% towards lithium-ion and sodium-ion cell manufacturing.
- For-profit organisations: Up to 70% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow), leaving at least 30% to cover.
- Non-profit legal entities: Up to 100% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow).

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
Apply for lithium-ion and sodium-ion cell manufacturing through the European Funding & Tenders Portal in one stage.
- Full proposal: 31 March 2027, 17:00 Brussels time. Submit Part A (online administration form) and Part B (technical proposal). Part B is limited to 40 pages.
- Opening: 3 December 2026.

cards.title: Project window
cards.answer:
The grant agreement (the contract setting the funded work and payment rules) sets the start date and duration for lithium-ion and sodium-ion cell manufacturing.
- Required start: Work normally starts after the grant agreement is signed. A reasoned exception needs approval.

funding_timing_submission.title: Application
funding_timing_submission.question: Mandatory information to include in the application

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
Conditional and exceptional requirements
cards.answer:
The cell-manufacturing call has conditions on controlling interests and commercial use of results.
- Conditional — Commercial exploitation: If results will be commercialised, include a strategy and a preliminary plan for scaling and deployment.
- Conditional — Satellite services: Use Copernicus for Earth observation and/or Galileo or the European Geostationary Navigation Overlay Service for satellite positioning, navigation or timing for satellite-based observation, positioning, navigation or timing.
- Expected: Report results to European Partnership on Batteries (the European industry and research initiative) against its performance indicators.
- Exception — Results transfers: The granting authority may object to transfers or exclusive licences (giving another party sole rights to use the results) of results for up to four years after project end.
